drhp.business: EL Forge Limited manufactures steel forgings, with the MD&A stating plainly that "the revenues are from the sale of forgings" and that there was no income from sale of land during the year. The company supplies the Indian automotive value chain and also exports, which exposes it to foreign exchange risk. Its in-house Tool Room and R&D effort is directed at value-engineered die design and manufacture, material wastage reduction and manufacturing efficiency on the shop floor.

risks.note: Management states directly under Opportunities & Threats that 'a faster shift to electric vehicles will have a impact on our business'. As a forgings supplier to the auto value chain, a powertrain change alters the content-per-vehicle the company sells; the MD&A itself notes electric PV volumes neared ~2 lakh units at ~4% penetration of PV sales in FY26 and that India is set to become the largest EV market by 2030.

Flagged verbatim: 'Under utilisation of the installed capacity resulting in increasing fixed costs of the company'. For a forging operation this is operating leverage working in reverse - the cost base does not fall with volume, so margin is exposed to any demand air-pocket. No installed-capacity or utilisation figure is disclosed anywhere in the routed text.
risks.risk: Under-utilisation of installed capacity raising fixed costs

risks.note: Under Commodity Price Risk: 'The Steel prices have increased substantially during the year and continues to be on the upward spiral.' Management says the increases are compensated from customers and that other input costs are negotiated case to case - so the risk is not price level itself but the timing and completeness of pass-through, and the MD&A separately warns that 'growing cost of key raw materials may impact revenues and profitability of the company'. Material cost was 57.83% of sale value for the year.

Flagged verbatim: 'Several new companies are entering the market, and existing rivals in adjacent product categories are also increasing their offerings.' This pressures both pricing and the ability to recover input-cost inflation from customers.
risks.risk: Competitive intensity from new entrants and adjacent players

risks.note: 'The Company is exposed to foreign exchange risks on account of its exports.' Mitigated by a formulated hedging strategy for foreign currency exposures, but the exposure is structural to the export share of the business. The MD&A separately names rising US tariffs and global trade pushback as headwinds.

The MD&A states that 'the revenues are from the sale of forgings' with no income from sale of land during the year - the company has one product line serving one cyclical end market, the Indian automotive industry, which the MD&A itself describes as a FY26 'tale of two halves' whose recovery depended on the September 2025 GST 2.0 rate cut.

The Risk Management paragraph names the key risks impacting the business as economic, foreign exchange, raw material, technology, funding, talent and cyber security. Talent is echoed in the HR narrative, which links training and development to facing competition and notes staff cost rose 'in order to maintain and retain talent with the company', against a base of only 146 employees on the rolls.
